rationale.overall: B matches the reference's chart-on-a-wide-datum read and stays legible when shrunk, which outweighs A's slightly closer glow.
rationale.material: A's orange reads as an emissive, light-bleeding rod with a warm bloom up the columns, closer to the reference's neon gel, while B's base looks more like a lit plastic capsule with a harder top specular and a cooler drop shadow.
rationale.silhouette: The reference's orange rule extends well past the outer columns, which B reproduces, whereas A's rule is inset and reads as a plinth cut to the bar group.
rationale.smallsize: At 32px and 16px B's longer, thicker baseline survives as a continuous stroke under all three bars, while A's shorter rod thins at the ends and loses that anchor.

rationale.overall: B is closer to the reference at full size: the orange reads as a glowing datum with light climbing the bars, not a shorter matte plinth, and that is the reference's whole read.
rationale.material: B's base emits into the bars and onto the porcelain with rim-lit charcoal edges, matching the reference's volumetric gel-and-neon lighting better than A's thicker, more shadow-weighted slab.
rationale.silhouette: B's thinner orange rule running past the outer bars matches the reference's chart-on-a-datum composition, while A's shorter, thicker plinth reads as a base cut to fit the bars.
rationale.smallsize: At 32px and 16px both strips still read as three dark columns on an orange line with similar contrast, and neither is clearly more legible once pixelated.
